name: Massachusetts
summary_text:
Travellers to Massachusetts stand under the United States federal framework for travel documents, visa decisions and airport screening. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary, barred transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with their gender identity, prohibited self-selection of gender on passports and visas, and directed the attorney general to correct the misapplication of Bostock v. Clayton County (2020). The Supreme Court allowed the resulting passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect in November 2025, superseding a State Department policy that had been in place since 1992.
 The State Department stopped processing the X marker and any marker not matching sex assigned at birth. New passport applications are processed only as M or F according to supporting documents, while passports already issued with an X marker remain valid until expiry. Trans and nonbinary travellers report passports confiscated or blocked at application, with some left stranded abroad. The ACLU has sued the State Department on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and Lambda Legal maintains guidance on what documentation to consider and how name and gender changes interact with federal records.
 Entry decisions follow the same federal line. Executive Order 14201 of 5 February 2025, and the State Department announcement of 25 February 2025 that followed it, mean that trans athletes seeking entry to compete in women's sporting events face visa refusal, and that declaring a gender other than sex assigned at birth at application may be treated as fraud carrying a permanent bar. These rules apply in Massachusetts as they apply in every other state.
 Airport screening carries an outing risk that state law does not reach. TSA procedures can involve secondary screening, devices and pat-downs that are invasive of privacy. Several foreign governments have responded to the document and data rules: in April 2025 CNN reported advisories about trans people travelling to the United States over identity-document and data rules, and Axios reported in March 2025 that at least eight European countries, including Finland and Denmark, adjusted travel guidelines for trans and nonbinary citizens entering the country.
 Massachusetts itself sits at the protective end of the national picture. A July 2026 national legal-risk assessment built from a rubric covering thousands of tracked anti-trans bills places the state in the fifteen-state "Most Protective" tier, alongside California, Colorado, Connecticut, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont and Washington, whose laws are described as having gone beyond the minimum in safeguarding trans rights.
 The state's shield law is directly usable by a visitor. The Massachusetts refuge provision protects patients and providers from civil or criminal charges when care that is legal here was banned in the home state, which matters to a traveller coming from one of the 27 states that ban gender-affirming care for children.

name: Michigan
summary_text: Michigan stands under the national framework of the United States. Executive Order 14168, in force since January 2025, redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary and requires federal identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth. The State Department stopped processing the X marker and issues new passports only as M or F on the supporting documents submitted. Passports already holding an X remain valid until expiry, but trans and nonbinary travellers report confiscation or blocked applications, with some left stranded abroad. The ACLU is suing the State Department on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and in November 2025 the Supreme Court allowed the department's passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect, superseding a policy in place since 1992.  Entry carries a second exposure. On 25 February 2025 the State Department announced that it would refuse visas to trans athletes seeking to enter the United States to compete in women's sporting events, flagging such applicants with an internal marking and treating a listed gender other than the one assigned at birth as grounds for a permanent ban for fraud. Screening at United States checkpoints can involve secondary screening, devices and pat-downs that are invasive of privacy, and several foreign governments have issued advisories about trans people travelling to the United States over identity-document and data rules.  State law in Michigan runs in the opposite direction to the federal posture. Governor Gretchen Whitmer signed the first major expansion of the Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act on 8 March 2023, codifying sexual-orientation and gender-identity protections into state statute, after a July 2022 Michigan Supreme Court ruling had already made such discrimination unlawful. The legislature banned conversion therapy in 2023 and outlawed the gay and trans panic defense in 2024.  A July 2026 national anti-trans legal risk assessment places Michigan in its Low-Risk States tier, alongside Nevada, finding that both have enacted fairly robust non-discrimination policies but fall short in ensuring healthcare equity and in providing protections for incarcerated transgender individuals. The same assessment designates the United States overall as Do Not Travel for transgender people, so the state-level rating does not offset the federal entry, document and screening risks.  In March 2025 the Michigan House passed a non-binding resolution urging the Michigan High School Athletic Association to bar transgender athletes from girls' and women's sports. The measure is advisory only and does not change state law or the state's non-discrimination protections.  Care access is constrained nationally. Executive Order 14187 of January 2025 described gender-affirming care for minors as chemical and surgical mutilation of children, in summer 2025 the Department of Justice subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for records of patients under 19, the federal government shut down specialised LGBTQ youth services on the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline in July 2025, and October 2025 proposed rules would bar Medicaid reimbursement for care to transgender patients under 18. Gender-affirming care for children is already banned in 27 states, and several of these federal measures have been blocked or enjoined in court.

sources.documents: Legalizes same-sex sexual activity in Michigan by invalidating state sodomy laws that applied to homosexuals and heterosexuals; article notes legislature has not repealed sodomy law.
